newsitem.title: USA: King ahead in run to Iditarod halfway point.
newsitem.headline: King ahead in run to Iditarod halfway point.

text.p: Defending champion Jeff King held a 47-minute lead over his nearest rival early Thursday as leaders began their march to the halfway point in the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race.

King, who won the 1,161-mile race in 1993 and 1996, left the former mining settlement of Ophir at 1:50 a.m. (5:50 a.m. EST). The checkpoint is 474 miles into the race course from Anchorage, and 90 miles before the ghost town of Iditarod that serves as the race's midway point.

Following King out of Ophir was 1995 champion Doug Swingley, followed 11 minutes later by two-time champion Martin Buser. Seven other top mushers, including Tim Osmar and DeeDee Jonrowe, departed Ophir in the next six hours.
The first musher to the halfway point in the race to Nome wins a $3,000 prize.
The Iditarod began Saturday with a ceremonial run in Anchorage. Timed competition began Sunday in Willow.
In the past two years, Iditarod champions have reached the Nome finish line in nine days. The winner gets $50,000 and a new truck, part of the total race purse of over $400,000.
Of the 53 mushers who began the Iditarod, two had dropped out as of Thursday.
